dossier.architecture: Turreted shooter with physics-based moving shots and truss-reacting traversal climb.

subsystems.drivetrain: Custom swerve; slip detection reduces trust in wheel odometry.
subsystems.intake: Rigid collector with elastic linkage that yields inward on impact.
subsystems.transfer: Separate horizontal and vertical conveyors; infrared/color sensors track cargo.
subsystems.scoring: Low-mounted two-motor turret transmission; adjustable hood and later top roller.
subsystems.endgame: Telescopic hook plus truss-reaction structure reaches traversal with few active steps; deployable line camera improves alignment.
subsystems.controls: Shot simulation selects trajectories insensitive to error; fused pose and radial/tangential velocity compensation support moving shots.

versions: Shooter rebuilt after first Israeli event to add top roller and reduce bounce-outs. Alignment camera added after approach time became a climb bottleneck.
dossier.analysis: Their advantage is the combined localization, shot model and mechanically repeatable feeder. A turret alone does not create accurate moving shots; alignment time can dominate an otherwise fast climber.
limits: Reported performance and prototype history are attributed to the source; not every intermediate revision is recoverable.

context_documents.title: 2022-1690 · Moving shots require a state model beyond distance alone
context_documents.body:
# 2022-1690: Moving shots require a state model beyond distance alone

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A compliant-link collector feeds horizontal/vertical conveyors and a low-driven turret. The source describes a shot model using distance and chassis velocity components to select hood angle and wheel speed.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The retained construction uses linkage compliance for impact survival; the interview explains compensating radial and tangential motion in the aiming solution.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A distance-only lookup cannot describe the same shot from a stationary robot and one moving sideways. The compensation still depends on measured release behavior and pose latency. A sophisticated model does not excuse uncontrolled incoming cargo state.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test moving-shot error by direction/speed, camera latency and worn cargo; compare predicted and measured flight time.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
